'''''Erica'' × ''darleyensis''''', the '''Darley Dale heath''', is a plant [[hybrid (biology)#In plants|hybrid]] between the heathers ''[[Erica carnea|E. carnea]]'' and ''[[Erica erigena|E. erigena]]'', probably of garden origin.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book | editor-last = Brickell | editor-first = Christopher | title = The Royal Horticultural Society A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants | year = 2008 | page = 302 | publisher = Dorling Kindersley | location = United Kingdom | ISBN = 9781405332965}}</ref>

It is a bushy shrub growing to {{convert|60|cm|in|abbr=off}} tall by {{convert|75|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad, with white to rose-pink urn-shaped flowers in late winter and early spring.

Unlike some plants in this genus, it has no particular requirement for [[soil pH|acid soil]] and grows in all soil types.<ref name=Proudley>{{cite book |author1=Brian Proudley |author2=Valerie Proudley |title=Heathers in Colour |date=1989 |publisher=Blandford Press |isbn=0713714204 |page=136 |edition=2nd |quote=Extremely hardy, they thrive in the worst of soils and flowering can be said to cover the whole of the winter period until late into the spring.}}</ref> It requires sharp drainage in full sun.<ref>{{cite web |title=Erica × darleyensis 'Darley Dale' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/91316/erica-darleyensis-darley-dale/details |website=[[Royal Horticultural Society]] |access-date=24 January 2025}}</ref> It is especially suitable as [[groundcover]], for instance as an underplanting for [[conifer]]s.

The seedling was found in a nursery in [[Darley Dale]], Derbyshire, UK, prior to 1900.<ref>{{cite web 
| url= https://www.heathersociety.org/heathers/erica-hardy/erica-x-darleyensis/darleyensis-corolla-pink/darley-dale/
